ISD.name: Improved Service Delivery
ISD.definition:
Improved Service Delivery measures the impact of initiatives that enhance the speed, reliability, accessibility, and overall quality of services provided to residents and internal customers. This includes faster response and resolution times, improved service consistency, clearer communication, reduced escalations or complaints, and more seamless end-to-end service journeys.

Value is realized when an initiative improves service outcomes, strengthens customer trust and satisfaction, increases predictability of service performance, or reduces friction in interactions — resulting in a more responsive, transparent, and user-centered service experience.

CC.name: Capacity Creation
CC.definition:
Capacity Creation captures the value generated by freeing up employee time and organizational capacity through the elimination, reduction, or automation of manual, repetitive, or low-value activities. This includes streamlining workflows, reducing handoffs, improving process reliability, and enabling staff to redirect effort toward higher-value, strategic, or resident-facing work.

Value is realized when an initiative measurably reduces effort or cycle time, increases throughput without additional staffing, or creates reusable capacity — typically quantified in hours saved, productivity gains, or increased workload absorption — without compromising service quality.

DCS.name: Direct Cost Savings
DCS.definition:
Direct Cost Savings reflects the tangible financial impact of initiatives that reduce current operating costs or prevent future expenditures. This includes targeted reductions in labour costs, vendor or contract spend, infrastructure and licensing expenses, rework, overtime, or other avoidable operational costs.

Value is realized when an initiative delivers measurable, attributable financial benefits — such as budget reductions, avoided cost growth, or deferred spend — expressed in dollar terms. Cost savings may occur independently or as a direct outcome of improvements in capacity creation, service delivery, or risk reduction.

kpis.name: Average Response Time
kpis.definition: Average time between receipt of a service request and first meaningful staff response. Captures how quickly the organization acknowledges and acts on resident or internal requests.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Speed of initial service acknowledgement
kpis.formula: (Sum of response times for all requests) ÷ (Number of requests in period)
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 Service Request system; departmental case management; email tracking
kpis.notes: Customize with service type — e.g. permit, complaint, enquiry

kpis.name: Average Resolution Time
kpis.definition: Average elapsed time from service request submission to full resolution or closure. Indicates service throughput and end-to-end efficiency.
kpis.whatItMeasures: End-to-end time to fully resolve a service request
kpis.formula: (Sum of resolution times for closed requests) ÷ (Number of requests closed in period)
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 system; SAP; ServiceNow or equivalent work order / case system
kpis.notes: Pair with ISD-001 to show full service journey

kpis.name: SLA Adherence Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of service requests resolved within the defined service level agreement (SLA) target timeframe. Key indicator of service reliability and consistency.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Proportion of requests meeting committed service standards
kpis.formula: (Requests resolved within SLA ÷ Total requests resolved) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 system; departmental SLA tracking; ServiceNow
kpis.notes: Requires defined SLA targets per request type

kpis.name: Resident / Client Satisfaction Score
kpis.definition: Average satisfaction rating collected from residents or clients following a service interaction. Reflects perceived service quality from the user's perspective.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Resident or client perception of service quality
kpis.formula: Average score from post-service survey (e.g. 1–5 scale or NPS 0–10)
kpis.suggestedSources: Post-service survey (MS Forms, phone survey); 311 feedback mechanism
kpis.notes: Requires active survey mechanism; sample size matters

kpis.name: First-Contact Resolution Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of service requests or enquiries fully resolved on the first interaction without requiring follow-up contacts or escalation.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Effectiveness of resolving issues without repeat contacts
kpis.formula: (Requests resolved on first contact ÷ Total requests) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 system; call centre platform; CRM system
kpis.notes: Requires flagging of repeat contacts in system

kpis.name: Service Complaint / Escalation Rate
kpis.definition: Rate of formal complaints or escalations received relative to total service interactions. Low rates indicate service quality; trend monitoring reveals emerging issues.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Frequency of service failures requiring escalation
kpis.formula: (Complaints or escalations ÷ Total service interactions) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 complaint log; Councillor office request tracking; departmental escalation log
kpis.notes: Distinguish formal complaints vs. informal feedback

kpis.name: Wait Time
kpis.definition: Average time residents or clients wait before receiving service — in-person, phone, or digital queue. Directly impacts resident experience and perceived quality.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Delay experienced before service begins
kpis.formula: (Sum of wait times across all interactions) ÷ (Number of interactions)
kpis.suggestedSources: Queue management system; walk-in service counters; phone system ACD reports
kpis.notes: Particularly relevant for in-person or phone services

kpis.name: On-Time Delivery Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of service outputs, decisions, or deliverables provided by the committed or legislated deadline. Applies to permits, reports, inspections, and time-bound outputs.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Proportion of outputs delivered by committed deadline
kpis.formula: (Outputs delivered on time ÷ Total outputs due in period) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Permit management system (Amanda); SAP project tracking; departmental schedule log
kpis.notes: Requires defined due-date field in tracking system

kpis.name: Digital / Online Service Adoption Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of total service transactions completed through digital or self-service channels vs. assisted channels. Indicates modernization and accessibility progress.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Shift toward digital service delivery
kpis.formula: (Digital transactions ÷ Total transactions) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Online portal transaction log; 311 channel mix report; departmental digital platform logs
kpis.notes: Distinguish between channel types in system

kpis.name: Service Accessibility — AODA Compliance Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of services, digital assets, or physical locations meeting AODA (Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act) compliance requirements. Measures inclusive service delivery.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Breadth of accessible, AODA-compliant service delivery
kpis.formula: (AODA-compliant services or assets ÷ Total services or assets audited) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Accessibility audit results; IT accessibility scans; facilities compliance reports
kpis.notes: Requires structured AODA audit process

kpis.name: Customer Effort Score (CES)
kpis.definition: Measures how much effort a resident or client had to exert to get their issue resolved or service completed. Lower effort scores indicate smoother, more user-friendly service experiences.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Ease of service interaction from the resident's perspective
kpis.formula: Average CES rating from post-interaction survey (typically 1–7 scale, lower = less effort)
kpis.suggestedSources: Post-service survey (MS Forms); call centre survey; web feedback widget
kpis.notes: Complements CSAT — measures process ease not just satisfaction

kpis.name: Service Request Volume Trend
kpis.definition: Month-over-month or year-over-year change in volume of service requests received. Tracks demand patterns and identifies seasonal spikes, emerging issues, or impact of prevention initiatives.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Direction and magnitude of change in service demand
kpis.formula: ((Current period volume − Prior period volume) ÷ Prior period volume) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 system; departmental case management system
kpis.notes: Use to contextualize other ISD metrics — e.g. satisfaction during high-volume periods

kpis.name: Repeat Contact Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of residents or clients who contact the city more than once for the same issue within a defined window. High repeat rates signal unresolved issues or poor first-contact quality.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Frequency of residents needing to re-contact for the same issue
kpis.formula: (Contacts flagged as repeat for same issue ÷ Total contacts) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 system; CRM with case linking; call centre platform
kpis.notes: Inverse of FCR — use together

kpis.name: Service Availability / Uptime
kpis.definition: Percentage of scheduled operating time during which a service, system, or facility is available and functioning as intended. Applies to digital systems, physical facilities, and field services.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Reliability and continuity of service access
kpis.formula: (Actual uptime hours ÷ Scheduled operating hours) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: IT system monitoring; facility booking system; field service schedule vs. actuals
kpis.notes: Define 'scheduled operating hours' clearly for each service context

kpis.name: Proactive Communication Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of service interactions or updates where the city proactively communicated status to residents without them needing to follow up. Reduces inbound contact volume and builds trust.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Frequency of outbound, proactive resident communication
kpis.formula: (Proactive notifications sent ÷ Total active service cases) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: 311 notification logs; email/SMS communication platform; CRM outbound tracking
kpis.notes: Requires notification tracking in case management system

kpis.name: Inspection / Site Visit Completion Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of scheduled inspections or site visits completed on time within the committed timeframe. Relevant for bylaw, building, environmental, and infrastructure inspection services.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Timeliness and completion of scheduled field inspections
kpis.formula: (Inspections completed on schedule ÷ Total inspections scheduled) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Inspection scheduling system; Amanda (permits); field service management system
kpis.notes: Subset of on-time delivery for inspection services

kpis.name: Hours Saved
kpis.definition: Total staff hours freed from manual, repetitive, or low-value activities as a result of the initiative. The primary quantitative measure of capacity creation value.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Volume of staff time reclaimed for higher-value work
kpis.formula: (Hours per task before − Hours per task after) × Volume of tasks per period
kpis.suggestedSources: Staff time tracking; before-and-after process timing study; payroll system
kpis.notes: Requires baseline measurement before initiative launch

kpis.name: Cycle Time Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in the end-to-end elapsed time for a defined internal process. Measures how much faster a process completes after improvement, independent of volume changes.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Speed improvement in completing an internal process
kpis.formula: (Cycle time before − Cycle time after) ÷ Cycle time before × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Case management system; SAP; workflow system timestamps
kpis.notes: Define process start and end points precisely before measuring

kpis.name: Automation Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of a defined set of tasks or transactions now handled automatically without manual intervention, as a result of the initiative.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Proportion of work handled by automated processes
kpis.formula: (Automated transactions ÷ Total transactions) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Automation platform logs; RPA dashboard; workflow system reports
kpis.notes: Requires transaction tagging in system — auto vs. manual

kpis.name: Throughput Rate
kpis.definition: Volume of work items processed per unit of time or per FTE. Measures organizational output capacity and productivity relative to staffing level.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Work output relative to staff time or resources
kpis.formula: Number of work items completed ÷ Staff hours worked in period
kpis.suggestedSources: Case management system; SAP; 311 system; departmental work queue reports
kpis.notes: Establish baseline period before initiative for comparison

kpis.name: Staff Utilization Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of available staff capacity actively deployed on productive work vs. idle, waiting, or administrative overhead. Indicates how effectively capacity is being used.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Productive use of available staff time
kpis.formula: (Productive hours worked ÷ Total available hours) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Time tracking system; HR scheduling records; manager estimation
kpis.notes: Requires time tracking or structured estimation methodology

kpis.name: Backlog Reduction Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage reduction in the volume of outstanding, aged, or unprocessed work items over a defined period. Indicates improved capacity to keep up with incoming demand.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Progress in clearing accumulated unfinished work
kpis.formula: (Backlog at start − Backlog at end) ÷ Backlog at start × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Work queue report; case management system; SAP aging report
kpis.notes: Define backlog threshold — e.g. items older than X days

kpis.name: Manual Effort Reduction Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage reduction in manual steps, handoffs, or effort required to complete a process after the initiative. Indicates process simplification and automation impact.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Degree of manual work eliminated from a process
kpis.formula: (Manual steps before − Manual steps after) ÷ Manual steps before × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Process documentation; workflow analysis; time-and-motion study
kpis.notes: Requires process mapping baseline — document before and after

kpis.name: Error Rate Reduction
kpis.definition: Percentage reduction in errors, rework incidents, or quality failures in a process. Errors consume capacity — reducing them frees staff time and improves reliability.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Quality improvement and elimination of rework
kpis.formula: (Error rate before − Error rate after) ÷ Error rate before × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Quality control log; rework tracking; system error or exception reports
kpis.notes: Requires error tracking baseline

kpis.name: Non-Value-Added Activity Reduction
kpis.definition: Percentage reduction in activities identified as non-value-added — e.g. duplicate data entry, unnecessary approvals, redundant reviews — following process improvement.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Elimination of waste activities from a process
kpis.formula: (NVA activities before − NVA activities after) ÷ NVA activities before × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Process mapping workshop output; lean / process review documentation
kpis.notes: Requires structured process mapping — e.g. value stream mapping

kpis.name: Staff Capacity Redeployment
kpis.definition: FTE hours or positions redirected to higher-value work as a result of efficiency gains. Demonstrates that reclaimed capacity is being actively used rather than simply absorbed.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Productive reuse of reclaimed staff capacity
kpis.formula: FTE hours redeployed to strategic or higher-value tasks in period
kpis.suggestedSources: HR workplan records; manager attestation; time tracking if available
kpis.notes: Requires intentional redeployment tracking — pair with CC-001

kpis.name: Process Step Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in the number of distinct steps, approvals, or handoffs in a defined process. Fewer steps mean faster throughput, less effort, and lower error risk.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Simplification of process complexity
kpis.formula: (Steps before − Steps after)
kpis.suggestedSources: Process documentation; workflow mapping; BPMN diagrams
kpis.notes: Document process maps before and after — count discrete steps

kpis.name: Meeting / Administrative Overhead Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in hours spent on meetings, internal reporting, or administrative tasks that do not directly contribute to service delivery. Frees capacity for resident-facing or strategic work.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Reduction in internal overhead consuming staff capacity
kpis.formula: (Admin or meeting hours before − Admin or meeting hours after) in period
kpis.suggestedSources: Calendar analysis; staff survey or manager estimation; time tracking
kpis.notes: Sensitive metric — frame carefully; focus on systemic reduction not individual behaviour

kpis.name: Training Time to Competency
kpis.definition: Average time for a new staff member or role-changer to reach defined competency in a process or system. Shorter onboarding times indicate better-designed processes and training materials.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Speed of knowledge transfer and staff readiness
kpis.formula: Average days from start of training to passing competency assessment
kpis.suggestedSources: HR learning system; training records; manager assessment logs
kpis.notes: Define competency threshold clearly before measuring

kpis.name: Rework Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of completed work items that required rework, correction, or reprocessing due to errors or incomplete information. Direct measure of first-time-right quality.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Frequency of work needing to be redone
kpis.formula: (Work items requiring rework ÷ Total work items completed) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Case management system; quality review logs; correction tracking
kpis.notes: Track rework reason codes to identify root causes

kpis.name: Queue Wait Time (Internal)
kpis.definition: Average time a work item spends waiting in a queue before being picked up for processing. Distinct from resident-facing wait time — this measures internal workflow delays.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Internal delay before work is actively processed
kpis.formula: (Sum of queue wait times for all items) ÷ (Number of items processed)
kpis.suggestedSources: Work queue system timestamps; case management; workflow tool
kpis.notes: Requires workflow system with queue timestamp tracking

kpis.name: Report Generation Time
kpis.definition: Time required to compile and produce a standard operational or management report. Automation and data infrastructure improvements typically reduce this significantly.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Efficiency of management reporting processes
kpis.formula: Average hours to produce a standard report (before vs. after initiative)
kpis.suggestedSources: Staff time tracking; IT reporting system logs; manager estimation
kpis.notes: Start with high-frequency reports — weekly or monthly operational reports

kpis.name: Knowledge Reuse Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage of service interactions resolved using documented knowledge base articles, templates, or standard procedures vs. requiring custom or ad-hoc effort. Higher reuse = less duplicated effort.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Extent to which documented knowledge eliminates repeated effort
kpis.formula: (Interactions resolved via knowledge base ÷ Total interactions) × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: Knowledge management system; ServiceNow KB analytics; SharePoint usage logs
kpis.notes: Requires knowledge base with usage tracking enabled

kpis.name: Annual Cost Savings
kpis.definition: Total measurable reduction in actual expenditure compared to prior year baseline or approved budget, directly attributable to the initiative. Primary financial metric for DCS value.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Year-over-year reduction in actual spending
kpis.formula: Baseline cost (prior year or approved budget) − Actual cost after initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP financial reports; approved budget documents; departmental cost centre reports
kpis.notes: Requires clear cost attribution to the initiative

kpis.name: Cost Avoidance
kpis.definition: Quantified costs that would have been incurred without the initiative but were prevented. Includes deferred capital, avoided hiring, avoided licensing, or prevented service failures.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Future costs prevented from occurring
kpis.formula: Projected cost without initiative − Actual cost with initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP; capital plan; vendor quotes; procurement records; staffing plans
kpis.notes: Document the counterfactual clearly — what would have happened without initiative

kpis.name: Operating Expense Reduction Rate
kpis.definition: Percentage reduction in total operating expenditure for a defined cost centre, program, or service area compared to baseline.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Overall reduction in running costs
kpis.formula: (Operating cost before − Operating cost after) ÷ Operating cost before × 100
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP cost centre reports; approved operating budget; Finance quarterly reports
kpis.notes: Use consistent scope — same cost centre and services across periods

kpis.name: Overtime Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in overtime pay expenditure attributable to process improvements, demand levelling, or automation that eliminated the need for overtime hours.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Reduction in premium-rate staff time costs
kpis.formula: Overtime $ in baseline period − Overtime $ in post-initiative period
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP payroll / HR reports; time tracking system; departmental payroll summaries
kpis.notes: Isolate overtime attributable to the specific process or area

kpis.name: Vendor / Contract Spend Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in vendor payments or contracted service costs achieved through renegotiation, consolidation, or substitution as part of the initiative.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Savings from vendor or contract changes
kpis.formula: Prior contract value − New contract value (annualized)
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP vendor payment records; procurement / contracts registry; Finance department reports
kpis.notes: Requires procurement involvement for attribution

kpis.name: Cost Per Transaction / Unit
kpis.definition: Average fully-loaded cost of delivering one unit of a defined service or processing one transaction. Enables efficiency comparison over time and benchmarking.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Unit economics of service delivery
kpis.formula: Total program cost in period ÷ Number of transactions or service units delivered
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP cost centre; 311 transaction volume; departmental workload tracking
kpis.notes: Define 'unit' precisely; use consistent cost boundary across periods

kpis.name: Vacancy / Attrition Savings
kpis.definition: Cost avoided by not backfilling a position that became unnecessary due to process automation or redesign. Applies to natural attrition or voluntary redeployment — not forced reductions.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Avoidance of staffing costs through process redesign
kpis.formula: Fully-loaded cost of position(s) not backfilled in period
kpis.suggestedSources: HR / Compensation data in SAP; position control records; departmental org charts
kpis.notes: Must be voluntary — do not conflate with layoffs or forced reductions

kpis.name: Energy Cost Savings
kpis.definition: Reduction in electricity, natural gas, fuel, or other energy expenditure resulting from efficiency improvements, equipment upgrades, or operational changes.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Financial savings from reduced energy consumption
kpis.formula: Energy cost in baseline period − Energy cost after initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: Utility billing records; building automation system (BAS); fleet fuel tracking in SAP
kpis.notes: Separate energy type (electricity vs. gas vs. fuel) for clarity

kpis.name: Maintenance Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in planned or reactive maintenance expenditure as a result of preventive programs, condition monitoring, asset management improvements, or contract renegotiation.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Reduction in asset or facility maintenance spending
kpis.formula: Maintenance cost in baseline period − Maintenance cost after initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP maintenance work orders; asset management system; infrastructure cost reports
kpis.notes: Separate planned vs. reactive maintenance for richer insight

kpis.name: Material / Supply Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in materials, supplies, or consumables costs achieved through bulk purchasing, supplier consolidation, specification standardization, or waste reduction.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Savings from procurement or materials management improvements
kpis.formula: Material spend in baseline period − Material spend after initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP procurement / purchasing records; inventory management system
kpis.notes: Exclude one-time purchases; focus on recurring supply categories

kpis.name: Infrastructure / Licensing Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in technology infrastructure, software licensing, or facilities costs resulting from consolidation, rationalization, or renegotiation.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Savings from IT or facilities cost optimization
kpis.formula: Baseline infrastructure or licensing cost − Post-initiative cost
kpis.suggestedSources: IT asset register; software licensing records; facility cost reports in SAP
kpis.notes: Often realized over a multi-year horizon — track annually

kpis.name: Paper / Print Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in printing, paper, postage, and physical document handling costs as a result of digitization, process automation, or policy changes.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Cost savings from reducing physical document handling
kpis.formula: Baseline print / paper / postage cost − Post-initiative cost
kpis.suggestedSources: Facilities / supplies procurement records; print management system; postage logs
kpis.notes: Often a secondary benefit of digital transformation initiatives

kpis.name: Processing Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in the total cost to process a transaction, application, or case — including labour, system, and overhead costs — following process improvement or automation.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Lower cost of processing individual transactions or cases
kpis.formula: Average processing cost before − Average processing cost after
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP cost centre; time tracking; volume data from case management system
kpis.notes: More granular than DCS-006 — focused on per-item processing cost

kpis.name: Billing Error Recovery
kpis.definition: Revenue recovered or losses avoided through correction of billing errors, duplicate payments, overbilling by vendors, or missed revenue items identified and corrected.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Financial recovery from billing accuracy improvements
kpis.formula: $ recovered or avoided through billing corrections in period
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP accounts payable / receivable; billing audit reports; vendor reconciliation records
kpis.notes: Requires billing audit or reconciliation process — often one-time then ongoing

kpis.name: Storage Cost Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in physical or digital storage costs — including records management, warehousing, document storage facilities, or cloud/server storage — following rationalization or digitization.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Savings from reducing physical or digital storage footprint
kpis.formula: Storage cost in baseline period − Storage cost after initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP facilities costs; IT cloud billing; off-site storage vendor invoices
kpis.notes: Include both physical and digital storage in scope

kpis.name: Agency / Contractor Premium Reduction
kpis.definition: Reduction in costs from replacing or reducing use of temporary agency staff or external contractors with permanent staff, automated processes, or insourced capacity.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Savings from reducing reliance on premium-cost external resources
kpis.formula: Agency or contractor spend in baseline − Agency or contractor spend after initiative
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP vendor payments; HR / workforce planning records; procurement contracts
kpis.notes: Track FTE equivalent alongside $ to show workforce planning impact

kpis.name: Revenue Recovery / Fee Optimization
kpis.definition: Additional revenue recovered or generated through improved billing accuracy, fee schedule updates, grant offsets, or recovery of previously uncollected amounts.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Improvement in cost recovery or revenue generation
kpis.formula: Revenue after initiative − Revenue in baseline period (same service scope)
kpis.suggestedSources: SAP revenue accounts; billing system; fee schedule documentation; grant records
kpis.notes: Distinguish new revenue vs. recovery of existing entitlements

kpis.name: Response time for permit applications
kpis.definition: Average time from submission of a complete building permit application to first decision (approval, refusal, or RFI). Customized from ISD-001 for PDBS.
kpis.whatItMeasures: Permit processing speed
kpis.formula: (Sum of days from submission to first decision) ÷ Number of permits decided in period
kpis.suggestedSources: Amanda permit management system; departmental permit tracking log
kpis.notes: Added during PDBS engagement — 2025-05. Review annually.
